title: Make incremental task-sync export and import proportional to the changed tasks instead of scanning all N
outcome: Make incremental task-sync export and import proportional to the changed tasks instead of scanning all N
acceptance: An ordinary export after a recorded exchange discovers the changed tasks from the indexed project-feed interval since that exchange (with a rebuildable affected-ids projection including tombstones for changes the feed doesn't attribute to a work item), and reads, decodes, writes or removes only those tasks' documents; unchanged task files are not read, rewritten or touched. project.json records the feed cut.

An ordinary incremental import goes through the Git commit path: the changed paths come from the diff of .engram/ between the last-applied source commit and the incoming commit, and only those blobs are read and decoded, plus project.json and the documents a change references. Unchanged task documents are not opened or parsed; deletions are applied. A plain directory import without that commit context is either bootstrap (empty basis) or an explicit, named rebuild.

A full scan happens only for bootstrap or an explicit, named rebuild. A missing, gapped, stale or inconsistent cursor or basis refuses with a named reason, never a silent full scan. Baseline and membership history come from an indexed per-task projection, not by loading every historical complete tree.

Retry and replay stay exact; a repeat of a completed exchange resolves its recorded receipt before reading any payload (zero document reads), returning that exchange's historical receipt even if local state has moved on.
The model-A path uses the same changed set; per-sync task-document I/O and decoding grow with the number of changes, not the project size or its history.

Tests on a fixture of at least 2,000 tasks with history (5 changed, 1 added, 1 deleted) count documents read, decoded and written, and graph nodes visited. Document I/O equals the change set, and graph validation visits only the touched closure, for export, import, repeat no-op and the reverse direction. New SQL structures are rebuildable projections; new immutable delta-exchange record kinds and transitions are append-only additions to the existing ledger, and no existing durable record changes shape or meaning.
